column12: Judgement on the denominator, and the weakest row in this file. Gazyva is dosed as a fixed course rather than to progression, so the engine's stock model is a poor fit however the rate is struck. The CLL course was chosen because it is the one labelled regimen that fits inside a year; first-line follicular lymphoma adds up to two years of 1,000 mg every two months on top of the same induction, and lupus nephritis is 4,000 mg in year one then 2,000 mg a year, both of which would raise the denominator and so raise the measured discontinuation. Read as a lower bound

column11: all of it, and the layer adds nothing. Both studies behind this unit are glofitamab studies in which obinutuzumab appears only as pretreatment: NCT04408638 (STARGLO) is glofitamab with gemcitabine and oxaliplatin against rituximab with gemcitabine and oxaliplatin, and NCT06806033 tests the glofitamab CRS profile. The Columvi label has required that dose since its accelerated approval: 'Pretreat with a single 1,000 mg dose of obinutuzumab intravenously 7 days before initiation of COLUMVI (Cycle 1 Day 1)' (DailyMed setid 3516e753-f064-4d30-9bd5-e3f2e143f75d, published 2026-07-02). Those pretreatment doses are already billed as Gazyva and are already inside the 986mm the asset reports: Gazyva's Medicare Part B beneficiaries rose from 4,364 in 2022 to 5,252 in 2024 alongside Columvi's launch (CMS Medicare Part B Spending by Drug), while Columvi itself recorded 280 Part B beneficiaries in 2024
column12: no pool is seeded, because a readout here would expand Columvi's label and not Gazyva's. The volume effect on Gazyva is real but it is a growth rate, not an indication, and the marketed line already carries it. The FDA has in any case refused the expansion these studies support: the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee voted 8-1 against second-line glofitamab plus GemOx in May 2025 and the agency issued a complete response letter for that sBLA on 2025-07-18 (Roche investor update, 2025-07-18), citing the lack of US patients in STARGLO

column11: the non-renal share, which is the whole point of this layer. Gazyva was approved for active lupus nephritis on 2025-10-20 (Roche investor update 2025-10-20; the label now reads 'for the treatment of adult patients with active lupus nephritis (LN) who are receiving standard therapy', DailyMed setid df12ceb2-5b4b-4ab5-a317-2a36bf2a3cda), and ALLEGORY was run in the patients that approval leaves out: it enrolled 303 adults with active SLE 'excluding proliferative or membranous lupus nephritis' (Furie RA, Dall'Era M, Vital EM, et al., 'Efficacy and Safety of Obinutuzumab in Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus', N Engl J Med 2026;395(3):243-254, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2516150, PMID 41789864). The lupus nephritis share of US SLE patients is 37.9%: 'There were 101,972 patients with evidence of SLE from January 2007 to October 2019. Of these patients, 38,679 (37.9%) had evidence of LN' (Dall'Era M, Kalunian K, Eaddy M, et al., J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(1), doi:10.18553/jmcp.2022.21496, PMID 36190835, Optum claims). 1 - 0.379 = 0.621
column12: the published range for the lupus nephritis share of SLE is wide, from about 20% in adult-onset disease to 40-75% in some series, and 37.9% is a claims-based US figure from the middle of it. Taking a higher share would shrink this layer and grow the part already inside the label. The narrowing to moderate-to-severe active disease despite standard therapy, which is what ALLEGORY enrolled, is not applied here; it is carried in the penetration peak below, as the Saphnelo rows do it, because no sourced US figure for that share was found

column11: a judgement carrying two things: the narrowing to moderate-to-severe active disease left out of eligible_pct above, and the competitive position. Non-renal SLE already has two approved biologics, Benlysta (belimumab) and Saphnelo (anifrolumab), and obinutuzumab arrives as a third with a strong but not transformational effect (SRI-4 response 76.7% against 53.5% on placebo at week 52, an adjusted difference of 23.1 points; NEJM 2026;395(3):243-254). Against that, the dosing is unusually light for a chronic autoimmune biologic - 1,000 mg at weeks 0, 2, 24 and 26 and then every six months - and Saphnelo's own penetration of the same pool is thin, 1,877 Medicare Part B beneficiaries in 2024
